subject: Performance qualification + customer-led load test handshake
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Duarte <elena.duarte@stargaze.ai>; ops-admin@stargaze.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance qualification + test next steps (post-call recap)

Hi Elena — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled and avoid surprises: 

Summary of what we heard you need:
- 95th percentile latency SLO: <= 250 ms for typical text generation paths (non-streaming)
- Sustained throughput goal: ~120 requests/sec with spikes to 240 rps for 5–10m windows
- Streaming behaviour: up to 60 concurrent streaming sessions, up to 6 tokens/sec average per stream (bursty token bursts possible)
- Auth & network: customer firewall will allow our test IPs; no mutual TLS planned right now

What we will provide from Redwood before the window:
- A k6 script that simulates your request mix + a short Locust scenario for streaming probes (attached: redwood_k6_profile_v1.js).
- Temporary test service account credentials and an allowlist template (attached).
- A short preflight checklist for the day-of warmup and smoke tests.

Ask / next steps for Stargaze ops:
1) Please confirm the CIDR(s) you can allow through your firewall and any change freeze windows.
2) Can you share the internal SRE contact + service-account email we should add to the allowlist?
3) Preferred test windows (we suggested Tue/Wed mornings PST) — please confirm a couple of options.

Our recommended execution plan (we can adapt):
- Warmup: 30 minutes ramp to 40% load with sampling.
- Stage 1: 60 minutes steady-state at 100 rps to validate latency stability.
- Stage 2: 30m ramp to peak 240 rps for burst validation, then 30m cooldown.
- Streaming probe: run concurrently during Stage 1 for 45 minutes to validate KV/cache & connection handling.

I attached the initial scripts and an allowlist template. Marissa will provision test accounts once we have your allowlist and service-account email.

If anything in the summary above is off, call it out and we’ll revise. Assuming alignment, please reply with: CIDRs, service-account email, and two preferred windows.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124
From: Elena Duarte <elena.duarte@stargaze.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance qualification + test next steps (post-call recap)

Thanks Logan — this is helpful and accurate. A few notes from our side: 

- CIDRs we can open: 34.217.128.0/20, 52.24.0.0/18 (we'll confirm exact /32s for the day but these are the ranges our infra team will accept).
- Service account to add: redwood-tests@stargaze-ops. We will give it access to the staging endpoint only.
- Change freeze: we prefer to avoid network changes during our Friday deploy window (Fridays 08:00–12:00 PDT).

Regarding mutual TLS: our security lead asked whether Redwood requires client certificates for the streaming endpoint. For this test we'll keep TLS termination on our side and not require client certs, but we'd like to validate the TLS handshake behaviour (SNI and ALPN negotiation) during warmup. Is that supported in your k6 script?

Preferred windows:
- Tue 2026-09-22, 09:00–12:00 PDT (preferred)
- Wed 2026-09-23, 08:00–11:00 PDT (backup)

I'm attaching a small Locust scenario our SRE uses for stream-like probes (stargaze_locust_scenario_v3.py) — it simulates connection churn and token bursts, so you may want to run it concurrently.

Elena
Elena Duarte
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Stargaze AI
elena.duarte@stargaze.ai

Elena — perfect, thanks for the details and the Locust scenario. Quick answers and confirmations: 

- k6 script supports TLS handshake validation and ALPN probing (we'll add an explicit TLS probe step during warmup).
- We'll use redwood-tests@stargaze-ops as the service account to add to the allowlist. Please add our IPs to the staging endpoint only — we will never run production traffic against that account.
- Test plan: we can run Tue 2026-09-22 09:00–12:00 PDT. Marissa will create the HubSpot activity and open a JIRA ticket for ops coordination (JIRA: PERF-719).

Attachments included from our side: redwood_k6_profile_v1.js, ip_allowlist_template.txt, test-account-readme.txt. Marissa: can you provision two test accounts (standard + high-concurrency) and share creds in a secure snippet by EOD tomorrow? Ben: can you run a quick smoke-run of the k6 profile against our staging cluster Thursday AM to sanity-check the script?

One more note on metrics: please expect token-level metrics and per-route p95/p99. We will provide a short dashboard link before the window so your SREs can follow along.

If all good, I'll mark the HubSpot task and send a calendar invite for Tue 09:00 PDT.

— Logan
